chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Allah did not leave the earth without a scholar (Imam); and were it not for that, the truth would not be distinguished from the falsehood.

key_terms.عَالِمٍ: scholar/Imam (one with divine knowledge and authority)

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah not leave the earth without an Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the Shia doctrine of *Istidrar* (divine continuity), asserting that God never leaves the earth without a *Hujjah* (proof) to preserve religious truth. It highlights the epistemological necessity of the Imam, as without his authoritative guidance, the distinction between *Haqq* (truth) and *Batil* (falsehood) would become ambiguous for the community. This concept is foundational to the Shia understanding of divine justice and the preservation of revelation.
